display.purpose: Page hero H1s and section H2s. Emphasis words inside display text switch to Copper-Bright italics.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, nav links, buttons, form labels — always uppercase, always tracked wide.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy and ledes. Never used for headings or labels.

mono.purpose: Any measured value: stat counters, table cells, line references, diagram status labels. Never prose.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: Dropdown menus and the baseline for any new floating/overlay surface (sanctioned direction: extend this neutral family for card/modal elevation).

shadows.name: risk-safe-glow
shadows.purpose: RESERVED. Safe/recovering risk state on the BI-failure animation only. Never decorative.

shadows.name: risk-danger-glow
shadows.purpose: RESERVED. Active-failure risk state on the BI-failure animation only. Never decorative.

motion.name: card-lift
motion.purpose: The system's one interactive-card motion signature (facet cards).

motion.name: border-flip
motion.purpose: Default hover treatment: a hairline border or dark background flips to Copper / Bone, no scale or shadow added.

motion.name: dropdown-reveal
motion.purpose: Nav dropdown fade + slight translateY reveal on hover/focus-within.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The site's one CTA style — copper background, sharp corners, flips to bone on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-block; font-family: 'Jost', sans-serif; font-size: 12.5px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #0A0A0B; background: #C9854F; padding: 15px 34px; border-radius: 2px; text-decoration: none; transition: background 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { background: #F7F5F1; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #C9854F; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Facet Card
components.description: The system's signature card: hairline border that flips to solid copper and lifts 4px on hover.

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Form field: onyx-on-charcoal, hairline border that shifts to a copper-tinted line on focus.
components.css: .ds-field-label { display: block; font-family: 'Jost', sans-serif; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #C9CACE; margin-bottom: 7px; } .ds-field-input { width: 100%; background: #0A0A0B; border: 1px solid rgba(201,202,206,.14); color: #F7F5F1; padding: 13px 15px; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; outline: none; transition: border-color 0.3s; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-field-input:focus-visible { border-color: rgba(173,106,61,.35); }

components.name: Eyebrow Label
components.description: The system's most consistent signature: a wide-tracked uppercase kicker preceded by a short copper rule line, opening every major section.
components.css: .ds-eyebrow { font-family: 'Jost', sans-serif; font-weight: 400; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.38em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #C9854F; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; } .ds-eyebrow::before { content: ''; width: 34px; height: 1px; background: #AD6A3D; }

narrative.overview:
MineTrans reads like the private office where a mine's risk gets weighed, certified, and sealed — not a marketing site dressed up to look serious. The palette is near-black onyx and charcoal, the type pairs an old-world serif (Playfair Display) for authority with a tightly-tracked uppercase sans (Jost) for procedure, and every number that matters — statistics, line references, table values, node status — drops into monospace (IBM Plex Mono) so it visibly reads as measured, not narrated. Copper is the one accent, used sparingly: a thin structural line, a single button, a label. The overall register is quietly luxurious — restrained and expensive-feeling rather than flashy — and it explicitly rejects the neon-glow, dense-dashboard energy of flashy fintech/crypto products. Nothing here should feel like it's trying to impress; it should feel like it's already trusted.

The system is presently flat by construction, and its one recurring piece of drama — a colored glow ring — is reserved exclusively for signaling risk state in the BI-failure animation, never used decoratively.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black onyx/charcoal surfaces with a single copper accent, used sparingly
Serif display headlines (Playfair Display) paired with heavily-tracked uppercase sans labels (Jost)
Numbers and data render in monospace (IBM Plex Mono) to read as measured fact, not prose
Sharp, small corner radii (2–4px) — nothing rounded enough to feel soft or consumer-app
Flat by default; the only chromatic glow is a reserved semantic for risk-state visualization

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: Copper is the only expressive hue in the system, used for identity, emphasis, and interaction. Failure Red is not a second accent; it is a reserved semantic exclusively for danger/error states. No screen should introduce a third hue.

rules.name: The Structure-vs-Voice Rule
rules.body: Base Copper (#AD6A3D) is for lines, dashes, and borders — things you register peripherally. Copper-Bright (#C9854F) is for anything meant to be read — labels, buttons, active emphasis.

rules.name: The Instrument Rule
rules.body: Any character that represents a measured value — a stat counter, a table cell, a line number, a node's status — renders in IBM Plex Mono. Regular prose never does, even when it contains a number inline.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Every section opens with an uppercase, wide-tracked (0.38em) Copper-Bright label, prefixed by a 34px Copper rule line. This is the system's most consistent signature — never omit the rule line, never tighten the tracking.

rules.name: The Reserved Glow Rule
rules.body: Colored glow shadows exist in exactly one place: signaling safe/danger risk state on the BI-failure diagram. Every other elevated surface uses a neutral black shadow or no shadow at all.

dos: Do keep Copper to a single accent role — never introduce a second hue for a new status or category.
Do render every measured number (stats, table values, line refs, status labels) in IBM Plex Mono.
Do open the eyebrow before major section headings with the 34px Copper rule line and 0.38em tracking.
Do use neutral black ambient shadows (starting from the Popover value) for any surface that needs to visibly lift — now sanctioned.
Do cap corner radius at 2px for buttons/CTAs and 4px for cards and text-bearing panels; reserve 6px for photographic/illustrative image containers only.
Do keep new full-bleed treatments (photo bands, engine panels) as the deliberate exception to the 1180px container, not the default.
donts: Don't add a colored/chromatic glow to any component outside the BI-failure risk visualization — a decorative colored glow anywhere else is exactly the generic AI-slop tell this system has explicitly rejected.

Don't reach for a thick colored left-border ("side-tab") treatment on cards or callouts — an older .block pattern still has one, but new work should follow the uniform hairline-border treatment instead.
Don't round corners past 4px on anything text-bearing (buttons, cards, inputs, nav) — soft/pill shapes read as consumer-app, not this system.
Don't style this as a bright, dense, neon fintech/crypto dashboard — the confirmed anti-reference.
Don't use Inter, Jost, or Playfair Display outside their assigned roles (body / label / display respectively).
Don't use Failure Red (#E04B4B) for anything but danger/error/failure signaling — it is not a decorative "warm" alternative to copper.
